crossRefs.note: He went forward a little, fell on his face, and prayed, saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away…
My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from helping me, and from the words of my groaning?
My God, I cry in the daytime, but you don’t answer; in the night season, and am not silent.
Save me, God, for the waters have come up to my neck!
Don’t hide your face from your servant, for I am in distress. Answer me speedily!
Draw near to my soul and redeem it. Ransom me because of my enemies.
Yahweh, the God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before you.
Let my prayer enter into your presence. Turn your ear to my cry.
Again he went away, and prayed, saying the same words.
Again he returned, and found them sleeping, for their eyes were very heavy, and they didn’t know what to answer him.
For we don’t have a high priest who can’t be touched with the feeling of our infirmities, but one who has been in all…
He, in the days of his flesh, having offered up prayers and petitions with strong crying and tears to him who was able…
though he was a Son, yet learned obedience by the things which he suffered.

parallels.note: Again he went away, and prayed, saying the same words.

translations.web: Again, a second time he went away, and prayed, saying, “My Father, if this cup can’t pass away from me unless I drink it, your desire be done.”
translations.bsb: A second time He went away and prayed, “My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, may Your will be done.”
translations.kjv: He went away again the second time, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, thy will be done.
translations.asv: Again a second time he went away, and prayed, saying, My Father, if this cannot pass away, except I drink it, thy will be done.
